name: Maize Yellow
lede: Maize Yellow is a pale, creamy yellow named for corn, carried in our library from Ridgway's 1912 color atlas and still echoed in RAL's industrial paint list.

sections.title: A corn color, twice recorded
sections.body:
Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate IV, hue 19, tone f, a scan of an aged printed plate rather than a fresh pigment [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classifies the same value as a brilliant orange yellow, about 3.9 units from that block's reference chip [2]. RAL's industrial list carries a related chip, RAL 1006, under its own numbering, close enough in hue that the two plainly share a family even though RAL gives no credit to Ridgway [1][3].

Maize, the word, names the plant itself; Ridgway's dictionary dates maize-family color words in English to 1886, carried forward from his earlier 1886 nomenclature into the 1912 atlas [1]. The library's nearest match for this exact value is [[pale-peach|Pale Peach]], about 8 units off, with [[beige|Beige]] the better-known relative at a wider distance [2][4]. Further along the same pale, warm stretch of the chart sit [[khaki|Khaki]] and [[tan|Tan]], both deeper and less yellow [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Maize Yellow covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 119 works, about one in two hundred, as photographed [5]. It peaks in the 1780s, in 10 of 430 paintings, at nearly three times the expected rate, and it is over-represented in paintings from Japan, Switzerland and the United Kingdom [5]. Its company on canvas is mostly other beiges and khakis, not brighter yellows [5]. These are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings read as screen colors, so the match records a resemblance, not a pigment [5].
